content.value_statement: Flutter features become difficult to maintain when UI, business logic, and data access are mixed. This skill organizes them into clear, testable layers.
actual_capabilities: Separates Flutter applications into UI, data, and optional domain layers.
Defines responsibilities for views, ViewModels, repositories, services, and use cases.
Proposes a hybrid project structure organized by feature and architectural type.
Provides a sequential checklist for implementing a new feature.
Demonstrates repository caching, model transformation, ViewModel state, and reactive views.
Guides constructor injection with provider or get_it.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance, not automated project generation or code migration.
It does not select a state management library beyond basic ChangeNotifier examples.
Its sample service omits production HTTP, error handling, authentication, and persistence details.
Teams must adapt the layer boundaries to application size and existing conventions.

use_cases.title: Structure a New Flutter Feature
use_cases.description: Map a feature into models, services, repositories, ViewModels, views, and dependency registrations before implementation.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Coupled Application
use_cases.description: Identify mixed responsibilities and move data access, state, and business rules into testable layers.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Architecture
use_cases.description: Create a shared project structure and implementation checklist for consistent feature delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a layered architecture for my Flutter feature: [feature]. List each model, service, repository, ViewModel, view, and dependency registration.

prompt_templates.title: Review Layer Responsibilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Flutter classes: [class summary]. Assign each responsibility to UI, data, or domain layers and explain any changes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Flutter feature description using MVVM and repositories: [description]. Provide a migration sequence that preserves behavior and supports testing.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complex Domain Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the architecture for [workflow] across [repositories]. Decide whether use cases are needed, define dependencies, state transitions, caching, retries, and test boundaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design involving multiple data sources

output_examples.input: Plan a profile feature that loads a user from an API and supports refresh.
output: Data layer: a profile service fetches API models, while a repository transforms and caches the user.
UI layer: a ViewModel exposes loading and user state, while the view renders state and sends refresh actions.
Dependencies: inject the service into the repository and the repository into the ViewModel.

output_examples.input: Should checkout pricing logic stay in the ViewModel?
output_examples.output: Move reusable pricing rules into a checkout use case. Keep presentation state in the ViewModel and data access behind repositories.

output_examples.input: Review a widget that calls an HTTP client directly.
output_examples.output: Move HTTP access into a stateless service. Add a repository for transformation and caching, then inject it into a ViewModel.

best_practices: Keep views focused on rendering, layout, animation, and forwarding user actions.
Return clean domain models from repositories and keep raw API models inside the data layer.
Add a domain use case only when business logic is complex, reusable, or spans repositories.
anti_patterns: Do not call HTTP clients, databases, or platform plugins directly from widgets.
Do not expose mutable ViewModel state that views can change without commands.
Do not add domain layers or abstractions when simple repository and ViewModel boundaries are sufficient.

faq.question: Does this skill require ChangeNotifier?
faq.answer: No. ChangeNotifier is the example, but another listenable state approach can preserve the same layer responsibilities.

faq.question: When should I add a domain layer?
faq.answer: Add it when business logic is complex, reused across ViewModels, or coordinates multiple repositories.

faq.question: How should files be organized?
faq.answer: Group UI code by feature. Group data and domain code by architectural type unless project conventions require another structure.

faq.question: Where should caching happen?
faq.answer: Place caching in repositories because they provide the single source of truth for domain data.

faq.question: Does the skill generate complete production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples. Production implementations still need error handling, authentication, persistence, tests, and application-specific decisions.

faq.question: Can I use provider or get_it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports constructor injection and mentions both packages as dependency registration options.
